pre_mortem: Irving's strongest counter-case is that CAR's 37% blitz rate compounds TB's negative passing EPA, creates failed drives and produces a deficit that removes rushing volume. His recent rushing production cannot guarantee carries in that script. Coker's strongest counter-case is his 228 recent air yards: limited targets can still produce more than 66.5 yards through one explosive catch, and TB has allowed 14 passes of 20-plus yards. Missing injury and alignment information could materially change either role. Both remain provisional leans rather than strong selections.
slip_story: One coherent candidate story is a competitive, run-centered game: CAR leads narrowly, Hubbard limits CAR's passing demand, and TB keeps feeding Irving against the weaker run defense. Both candidates survive that base case; Irving also benefits if TB leads, but Coker's under is more fragile in that flip. Do not force a 3–4-leg slip from only two supported candidates.
